Match reference episodes to alarms

tl_match.Rd

Pairs reference episodes with detector alarms under a named policy and records the overlap behind every decision.

Usage

tl_match(ledger, policy = c("one_to_one", "any_overlap"),
  scope = c("full", "answered"), min_overlap = 0, min_episode_time = 0,
  learning_period = 0, episode_merge_gap = 0, alarm_merge_gap = 0,
  alarm_min_duration = 0)

Arguments

ledger

A tl_ledger.

policy

"one_to_one" or "any_overlap".

scope

"full" or "answered"; see Eligibility.

min_overlap

Pairs need overlap strictly greater than this.

min_episode_time

Minimum counted event time for eligibility.

learning_period

Time at the start of each record excluded from matching (episodes are clipped; alarms ending inside it are set aside).

episode_merge_gap,alarm_merge_gap,alarm_min_duration

Passed to tl_episodes() and tl_alarms().

Details

Overlap. The overlap between an episode and an alarm is the ledger time on which the reference is the event, the row belongs to the episode, and the detector response is positive. Intervals that only touch (one ends where the other starts) have zero overlap.

Eligibility. With scope = "full", an episode is eligible when its reference-known event time after the learning period is at least min_episode_time. With scope = "answered", the time counted is event time on which the detector answered (positive or negative). Ineligible episodes are kept in the output with the reason.

Policies.

  • "any_overlap": an episode is detected when any alarm overlaps it by more than min_overlap; an alarm is matched when it overlaps any eligible episode. One alarm may detect several episodes, and several alarms may share one episode. This is the rule used by WFDB epicmp for AF episodes (see wfdb_epicmp_af() for the full compatible procedure).

  • "one_to_one": each episode is matched to at most one alarm and each alarm to at most one episode. Pairs are eligible when their overlap exceeds min_overlap. The matching maximises the number of pairs, then the total overlap; remaining ties are broken towards pairs that occur earlier in time. Because neither episodes nor alarms overlap among themselves, the candidate pairs never cross in time, and the optimum is found exactly by dynamic programming over the time-ordered pairs.

Alarms are classified as "matched", "redundant" (overlaps an eligible episode but was not paired, which happens only under "one_to_one", e.g. a second alarm during one episode), "false" (no overlap with any reference event), "ineligible_overlap" (overlaps only ineligible episodes), "unassessable" (no reference-known time) or "learning_period".

Latency is the time from the episode onset to the issue time of the first positive decision of the matched alarm inside the episode. It is reported only when the onset was observed, the detector was answering at the onset, and issued_at was supplied. When the alarm was already active at the onset (a decision issued before the onset still holds), latency is not defined and latency_status is "alarm already active at onset". Otherwise latency is NA and latency_status says why.

Value

An object of class tl_match: a list with episodes (one row per episode and detector), alarms, pairs and settings.

Examples

fx <- tl_fixture("acceptance")
led <- tl_ledger(fx$records, fx$reference, fx$predictions,
                 time_unit = "min")
m <- tl_match(led)
m$episodes
#>   episode_id record start end event_time n_fragments onset_status offset_status
#> 1  rec1:e001   rec1    10  20         10           1     observed      observed
#> 2  rec1:e002   rec1    40  60         20           1     observed      observed
#>     members detector counted_time eligible eligibility_reason detected
#> 1 rec1:e001        D           10     TRUE               <NA>     TRUE
#> 2 rec1:e002        D           20     TRUE               <NA>    FALSE
#>      alarm_id overlap n_alarms latency         latency_status
#> 1 rec1:D:a001      10        1      NA issued_at not supplied
#> 2        <NA>       0        0      NA           not detected
m$alarms
#>      alarm_id record detector start end positive_time known_time issued_at
#> 1 rec1:D:a001   rec1        D    10  20            10         10        NA
#> 2 rec1:D:a002   rec1        D    70  80            10         10        NA
#>    status episode_id overlap
#> 1 matched  rec1:e001      10
#> 2   false       <NA>       0
